Your illustrated herb garden

Choose an herb to read its information and connect it to your splicing experiments. These new portraits match the named herbs; the original landscapes and fantasy plants remain in the image gallery.

AI-generated botanical illustrations, not a plant-identification guide. Growing facts are sourced below. Splice presets are fictional game combinations, not real gene edits or measured herb tolerances.

Basil

Ocimum basilicum

Plant features
Smooth broad green leaves; aromatic annual.

Grow it
Sun, fertile well-drained soil, regular water; protect from cold.

Common uses
Tomato dishes, soups and herb butter.

Harvest
Pinch young stem tips to encourage branching.

Game connection
Broad leaves and fast growth inspire a high-growth splice.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Rosemary

Salvia rosmarinus

Plant features
Woody evergreen with narrow needle-like leaves.

Grow it
Full sun and good drainage; overwinter indoors where winters are too cold.

Common uses
Use sparingly with poultry, fish and other savory dishes.

Harvest
Snip tender tips as needed.

Game connection
Narrow foliage inspires a water-conserving leaf choice; the game preset is fictional.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Thyme

Thymus vulgaris

Plant features
Small oval leaves on low woody stems.

Grow it
Full sun, excellent drainage; avoid soggy soil.

Common uses
Soups, stews and stuffing; fresh or dried.

Harvest
Cut stems; dry small bunches with airflow.

Game connection
Small leaves inspire water conservation and a compact, resilient strategy.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Sage

Salvia officinalis

Plant features
Gray-green textured leaves on a shrubby perennial.

Grow it
Full sun; very well-drained soil, especially in winter.

Common uses
Savory vegetables, poultry and stuffing.

Harvest
Pick leaves as needed; dry stems for storage.

Game connection
Textured leaves inspire resilient tissues in the fictional model.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Spearmint

Mentha spicata

Plant features
Serrated opposite leaves; spreads through underground stems.

Grow it
Sun to light shade; contain spreading roots in an above-ground pot.

Common uses
Beverages, jellies and savory sauces.

Harvest
Cut stems regularly for fresh young growth.

Game connection
Vigorous growth inspires the rapid-growth setting; real mint is not a dune plant.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Oregano

Origanum vulgare

Plant features
Small oval aromatic leaves; perennial herb.

Grow it
Full sun and well-drained soil; hardiness varies by type.

Common uses
Pizza, tomato sauces, soups and salads.

Harvest
Snip tips before flowering, leaving leaves to regrow.

Game connection
Small leaves inspire a resilient, water-conserving preset.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Flat-leaf parsley

Petroselinum crispum

Plant features
Flat divided leaves; biennial usually grown as an annual.

Grow it
Moist, well-drained soil; tolerates some shade.

Common uses
Soups, vegetables and garnish.

Harvest
Cut leaves once established; can be frozen.

Game connection
Taproot and leafy growth inspire a balanced growth preset.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Cilantro / coriander

Coriandrum sativum

Plant features
Lobed leaves; cilantro leaves and coriander seeds are one plant.

Grow it
Sun, well-drained soil; sow successive crops as plants bolt.

Common uses
Salsa and Mexican or Asian dishes.

Harvest
Pick leaves; let seed heads brown for coriander.

Game connection
A taproot and brief leafy season inspire the deep-root and growth choices.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Dill

Anethum graveolens

Plant features
Fine feathery leaves with yellow flower umbels.

Grow it
Sun and well-drained soil; direct sow to avoid transplant disturbance.

Common uses
Leaves and seeds flavor pickles and other foods.

Harvest
Snip foliage; collect mature seeds separately.

Game connection
Divided foliage inspires a smaller-leaf experiment; not a claim of pine-like physiology.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Chives

Allium schoenoprasum

Plant features
Tubular onion-flavored leaves with round purple flower heads.

Grow it
Sun and well-drained soil; divide clumps to propagate.

Common uses
Fresh leaves flavor sauces, salads and potatoes.

Harvest
Clip leaves; allow the clump to regrow.

Game connection
Clumping growth inspires fibrous roots and a regrowing strategy.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

English lavender

Lavandula angustifolia

Plant features
Narrow gray-green leaves and purple flower spikes.

Grow it
Full sun, exceptional drainage and airflow; drought tolerant once established.

Common uses
Fragrant dried sachets; culinary lavender is used sparingly.

Harvest
Cut flower stems as blooms begin opening.

Game connection
Dry-site adaptation inspires water retention and resilient tissues.
My herb notes
Source: Illinois Extension ↗

Lemon balm

Melissa officinalis

Plant features
Textured serrated green leaves with lemon fragrance.

Grow it
Sun to partial shade; moist, well-drained soil; remove seed stalks to limit spread.

Common uses
Fruit dishes, salads, teas and vinegars.

Harvest
Cut leafy stems, preferably before flowering.

Game connection
Leaf growth inspires a vigorous preset; no medicinal effects are simulated.
